findings.statement: Causal EDA persistence transfers to held participants better than registered drift/flexible controls

reliability.rationale: Persistence0.490197 microSiemens beats flexible0.542012 and all five physiological extensions on six held people. This supports a bounded null result. Claim-specific scope: Causal EDA persistence transfers to held participants better than registered drift/flexible controls

mechanism.rationale: Slow EDA memory does not isolate sweat physiology, mental stress, temperature effects or motion artifacts. Signed source values are preserved.

novelty.rationale: Primary-source analyses and established equation families are disclosed. This review does not establish exhaustive literature novelty or a new universal law.

significance.rationale: Useful as a transparent bounded research/evaluation case. Only aerobic protocol; S11 linked breaks held together; alignment uses each native sensor clock/rate; no narrow population confidence or clinical benefit.

reproducibility.rationale: Exact task, equation/state, group evidence, native semantics and provenance inspected; separate computational review is responsible for complete replay.

impact.rationale: No independent deployment, intervention, cost saving or clinical/industrial acceptance outcome was measured.

reliability.rationale: All saved predictions and primary metrics independently reproduce from source-verified inputs, including unfavorable alternatives. Conductance is a wearable measurement, not a directly observed stress mechanism or clinical endpoint.
